post.description:
Prices the swap as the quote does, builds the transaction `source` signs, stores it as `PENDING` and emits `SWAP_CREATED`. info.title: Cosmos Pay Payments API
info.description: Payments API for merchants and wallets. It covers: payment intents on Stellar, Solana and Monad (with payment links, customers and a product catalog); swaps (Stellar path payments, Solana via Jupiter, Monad via Kuru Flow), cross-chain swaps across Stellar, Solana, Monad and other networks through NEAR Intents, and USDT0 transfers from Stellar to EVM networks through LayerZero; private payments with a hidden amount on Stellar; Stellar liquidity pools and DeFindex yield vaults; fiat on/offramp and KYC through BlindPay; and webhooks that notify your server of payment events. Liquidity pools, DeFindex, USDT0, private payments and the SEP-10 and SEP-30 routes are Stellar only. Paths already include the version (`/v1/...`). Pick the matching server and security scheme below. **Every failure returns the same envelope** (`ApiErrorBodyEntity`), and `code` is the part to branch on: `message` is prose and may be reworded. Each operation documents only the statuses it can really return: `429` appears where a budget is declared (the budget itself is published as `x-cosmos-rate-limit`), `502`/`503`/`504` where the route calls a provider (`x-cosmos-upstream`), and neither `401` nor `403` on the probes that need no credentials (`x-cosmos-public`). **Every operation says who may call it.** On a route that takes an API key, the description ends with the scope the key must hold, also published as `x-cosmos-scopes` (all of) and `x-cosmos-scopes-any` (one of); a key with the `admin` role passes every scope check, and `x-cosmos-public-key` marks the routes the shared public key may call. A route that takes no API key (`x-cosmos-public`) says in its description how it is called. Authenticate every request with your secret API key in the `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` header.

code.description: The five-digit code the person read off the old device. A malformed one is a 400 and costs no attempt; a wrong one costs one of five.
